# Kirby Corporation Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results


by[Sarah Hudgins](https://kirbycorp.com/author/sarah-hudgins/)


| Oct 28, 2026


|[Press Releases](https://kirbycorp.com/category/press-releases/)


[PDF Version](https://kirbycorp.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2026-Q3-Earnings-Press-Release-vF.pdf)


- Third quarter 2026 earnings per share of $2.09, up 27% year-over-year
- Marine transportation revenues increased 17% year-over-year as market fundamentals continued to improve, driven by strong customer demand
- Distribution and services revenues grew 6% year-over-year, driven by robust demand for behind-the-meter and backup power solutions
- Returned $112 million of capital to shareholders through share repurchases during the third quarter of 2026
- Entered into an agreement to acquire certain inland marine assets from undisclosed sellers for $115 million, including nine inland towboats, 14 inland tank barges, nine bow thrusters, and a fleeting operation serving the Corpus Christi area
- Updated full-year earnings per share growth guidance range of 10% to 15% based on current outlook


HOUSTON, October 28, 2026 – Kirby Corporation (“Kirby” or “the Company”) (NYSE: KEX) today announced net earnings attributable to Kirby for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, of $110.8 million, or $2.09 per share, compared with earnings of $92.5 million, or $1.65 per share, for the 2025 third quarter. Total revenues for the 2026 third quarter were $977.2 million compared with $871.2 million for the 2025 third quarter.


David Grzebinski, Kirby’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our third quarter results reflected strong continued momentum across both businesses and solid execution throughout the organization. In marine transportation, strong barge utilization and favorable pricing trends supported performance during the quarter, though rising fuel costs continued to impact margins. In distribution and services, results benefited from robust demand in power generation and the strong growth of behind-the-meter solutions. Overall, the company executed well during the quarter and delivered solid financial and operating results, reflecting our continued focus on safety and operational excellence.”


“In inland marine, market fundamentals remained constructive during the quarter. Strong refinery operating rates, healthy petrochemical activity, and limited new industry capacity supported barge utilization in the low-90% range. Spot market rates improved sequentially in the low- to mid-single-digit range during the quarter, and term contract renewals increased in the low-single-digits compared with the prior year. Rising fuel costs remained a near-term headwind as higher costs were mitigated but not fully offset by cost escalators and rate recovery mechanisms in the quarter. Overall, the inland business delivered margins in the 20% range driven by a combination of steady demand, disciplined execution and limited industry capacity additions.”


“In coastal marine, customer demand remained stable with barge utilization in the high-90% range while third quarter coastal revenues increased slightly year-over-year. We had one contract renewal in the third quarter with an increase in the low-double-digit range. Operating margins were in the mid-teens range reflecting market specific dynamics and ongoing cost pressures.”


“In distribution and services, results reflected favorable market conditions for power generation and strong execution by our commercial and operational teams. Third quarter revenues increased 6% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for behind-the-meter and backup power generation solutions and a healthy environment for commercial and industrial.” Mr. Grzebinski concluded.


**Segment Results – Marine Transportation**
Marine transportation revenues for the 2026 third quarter were $568.7 million compared with $484.9 million for the 2025 third quarter. Operating income for the 2026 third quarter was $111.9 million compared with $88.6 million for the 2025 third quarter. Operating margin for the 2026 third quarter was 20% compared with 18% for the 2025 third quarter.


In inland marine, average barge utilization was in the low-90% range during the third quarter of 2026. Average spot market rates increased in the low- to mid-single-digit range sequentially during the quarter, reflecting improving market fundamentals. Term contract renewals increased in the low-single-digit range on average compared with the prior year. The inland market represented 81% of segment revenues in the third quarter of 2026. Inland operating margins were in the 20% range despite the impact of ongoing fuel cost headwinds.


In coastal marine, market activity remained strong, with barge utilization in the high-90% range. Coastal marine revenues increased slightly year-over-year and operating margins were in the mid-teens range, primarily reflecting fewer shipyard days compared to the second quarter of 2026. Coastal marine had a single term contract renewal in the third quarter with an increase in the low-double-digit range. Coastal marine represented 19% of segment revenues in the third quarter of 2026.


**Segment Results – Distribution and Services**
Distribution and services revenues for the 2026 third quarter were $408.5 million compared with $386.2 million for the 2025 third quarter. Operating income for the 2026 third quarter was $48.4 million compared with $42.7 million for the 2025 third quarter. Operating margin was 12% for the 2026 third quarter compared with 11% for the 2025 third quarter.


In the power generation market, revenues increased 8% and operating income increased 13% compared with the 2025 third quarter, reflecting continued demand for behind-the-meter and backup power solutions and solid execution even as OEM supply conditions remained dynamic. Order activity continued to strengthen, driven by demand from data center and industrial customers. Power generation represented approximately 46% of segment revenues for the quarter, with operating margins in the low-double-digit range.


In the commercial and industrial market, revenues increased 8% and operating income increased 23% compared with the 2025 third quarter, primarily reflecting strong marine repair activity and healthy demand across other industrial end markets. Commercial and industrial represented approximately 44% of segment revenues for the quarter, with operating margins in the low-double-digit range.


In the oil and gas market, revenues decreased 9% and operating income decreased 15% compared with the 2025 third quarter; however, revenues were flat and operating income was up 54% sequentially driven by higher-margin parts and service activity and ongoing cost management. Oil and gas revenues represented approximately 10% of segment revenues for the quarter, with operating margins in the low-double-digit range.


**Acquisition of Inland Marine Assets**
During the third quarter, Kirby entered into an agreement to acquire certain inland marine assets from undisclosed sellers for $115 million. The acquisition includes nine inland towboats, fourteen inland tank barges, nine bow thrusters, and a fleeting operation in Rockport, Texas, which is located on a 65-acre facility serving the Corpus Christi area. The acquired assets will enhance Kirby’s inland marine network in South Texas, expand fleeting and fueling capabilities near Corpus Christi, and support continued demand in the West End linehaul system. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to customary closing conditions.


**Financial Highlights**
For the 2026 third quarter, EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $229.7 million compared with $201.4 million for the 2025 third quarter. During the quarter, net cash provided by operating activities was $143.5 million, and capital expenditures were $69.5 million, resulting in free cash flow (non-GAAP) of $74.0 million. Working capital remained elevated during the quarter, reflecting higher revenues in both segments, timing of collections, and higher fuel-related receivables in marine transportation.


In the 2026 third quarter, Kirby returned $112 million of capital through share repurchases at an average share price of $137.04. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $38.3 million of cash and cash equivalents and $530 million of liquidity available. Total debt was $1,072 million and the debt-to-capitalization ratio was 23.7%.


**2026 Outlook**
Commenting on the outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026, Mr. Grzebinski stated, “As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, we remain encouraged by the momentum across our businesses. Driven by strong operational execution and favorable market conditions, we believe Kirby is well positioned to capitalize on opportunities across our end markets and deliver solid performance in the remainder of the year. Despite ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, customer demand remains healthy across many of our end markets. Based on current market conditions, we are narrowing our full-year earnings per share growth guidance to 10% to 15% and currently expect results toward the upper end of the range.”


In inland marine, market fundamentals are expected to remain constructive, supported by robust supply-demand dynamics and strong refinery and petrochemical operating rates. Barge utilization is expected to remain in the low-90% range, while both spot pricing and term contract renewal rates are expected to improve further during the remainder of the year. Inland operating conditions are expected to reflect normal seasonal weather impacts during the fourth quarter. Overall, inland revenues are expected to grow in the low-double-digit range, with operating margins expected to be in the high-teens to low-20% range for the full year.


In coastal marine, customer demand remains stable with barge utilization expected to remain in the high-90% range. Overall market conditions remain constructive, and pricing trends continue to improve, although elevated planned shipyard activity and higher fuel costs are expected to pressure margins during the fourth quarter. Overall, revenues are expected to increase in the mid-to-high-single-digit range for the full year, with operating margins expected to be in the mid-teens range.


In distribution and services, continued growth in power generation and strong marine repair activity are expected to support full-year results. In power generation, order momentum remains strong, supported by data center demand and the need for behind-the-meter and backup power solutions. While OEM engine delivery timing continues to create some variability in quarterly results, underlying customer demand remains robust. In commercial and industrial, customer activity is expected to remain healthy driven by strong demand in marine repair. In oil and gas, activity is expected to remain stable, subject to changes in the market environment. Overall, the Company expects segment revenues to grow in the high-single-digit range for the full year, with operating margins in the high-single-digit range.


The Company expects to generate net cash provided by operating activities of $575 million to $675 million in 2026 and capital spending is expected to range from $220 million to $260 million. Approximately $170 million to $210 million is expected to be allocated to marine maintenance capital and improvements to existing inland and coastal marine equipment, and facility improvements. Up to approximately $65 million is expected to be allocated to growth capital spending across both of our businesses.

**GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures**
The financial and other information to be discussed in the conference call is available in this press release and in a Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. This press release and the Form 8-K includes a non-GAAP financial measure, EBITDA, which Kirby defines as net earnings attributable to Kirby before interest expense, taxes on income, and depreciation and amortization. A reconciliation of EBITDA with GAAP net earnings attributable to Kirby is included in this press release. This press release also includes non-GAAP financial measures which exclude certain one-time items, including earnings before taxes on income (excluding one-time items), net earnings attributable to Kirby (excluding one-time items), and diluted earnings per share (excluding one-time items). A reconciliation of these measures with GAAP is included in this press release. Management believes the exclusion of certain one-time items from these financial measures enables it and investors to assess and understand operating performance, especially when comparing those results with previous and subsequent periods or forecasting performance for future periods, primarily because management views the excluded items to be outside of Kirby’s normal operating results. This press release additionally includes a non-GAAP financial measure, free cash flow, which Kirby defines as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures. A reconciliation of free cash flow with GAAP is included in this press release. Kirby uses free cash flow to assess and forecast cash flow and to provide additional disclosures on the Company’s liquidity. Free cash flow does not imply the amount of residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures as it excludes mandatory debt service requirements and other non-discretionary expenditures. This press release also includes marine transportation performance measures, consisting of ton miles, revenue per ton mile, towboats operated and delay days. Comparable marine transportation performance measures for the 2025 year and quarters are available in the Investor Relations section of Kirby’s website, www.kirbycorp.com, under Financials.

**About Kirby Corporation**
Kirby Corporation, based in Houston, Texas, is the nation’s largest domestic tank barge operator, transporting bulk liquid products throughout the Mississippi River System, on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, and coastwise along all three United States coasts. Kirby transports petrochemicals, black oil, refined petroleum products, and agricultural chemicals by tank barge. In addition, Kirby participates in the transportation of dry-bulk commodities in United States coastwise trade. Through the distribution and services segment, Kirby provides equipment, after-market parts and services for power generation systems in applications that include behind the meter power systems and emergency backup systems, after-market and genuine replacement parts and services for engines, transmissions, reduction gears, electric motors, drives, and controls, specialized electrical distribution and controls systems, and related equipment used in power generation, marine, on-highway, oilfield services, and other industrial applications. Kirby also rents equipment including generators, industrial compressors, high-capacity lift trucks, construction equipment, and refrigeration trailers for use in a variety of industrial markets. Kirby also manufactures and remanufactures specialized equipment, including pressure pumping units and electric fracturing systems, electric power generation equipment, and specialized electrical distribution and control equipment for data centers, oilfield service, railroad, and other industrial customers.
